title: Tensor closure for bounded-above pseudo-coherent complexes
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $K,L\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For integers $n,m$, suppose that $K$ is $n$-pseudo-coherent and $H^i(K)=0$ for $i>a$, while $L$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent and $H^j(L)=0$ for $j>b$ (where pseudo-coherence and its finite-stage variants are as in [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] and [def-pc-ring-m-pseudo-coherent]). Here $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L$ is the derived tensor product: the image in $D(R)$ of the direct-sum total tensor complex $\operatorname{Tot}(P^\bullet\otimes_R L^\bullet)$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], for any K-flat complex [def-pc-module-kflat-complex] $P^\bullet$ with a quasi-isomorphism $P^\bullet\to K$ and any complex $L^\bullet$ representing $L$. Then $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L$ is $t$-pseudo-coherent for $t=\max(m+a,n+b)$. In particular, the derived tensor of two pseudo-coherent objects is pseudo-coherent.

proof.text: Put $t=\max(m+a,n+b)$. The cited upper-bound theorem gives $H^i(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)=0$ for $i>a+b$. If $n>a$, then $t\ge n+b>a+b$; if $m>b$, then $t\ge m+a>a+b$. In either case the zero bounded finite-free complex maps to the tensor, is an isomorphism on cohomology above $t$ and surjective at $t$, and witnesses $t$-pseudo-coherence. Hence assume $n\le a$ and $m\le b$.

proof.text: Choose bounded finite-free witnesses $\alpha:P\to K$ and $\beta:Q\to L$ for the two finite-stage pseudo-coherence hypotheses. For $j>b$, one has $j>m$, so $H^j(\beta)$ is an isomorphism and $H^j(Q)=H^j(L)=0$. Thus $K$ and $Q$ have the upper cohomological bounds $a,b$ required by the tensor approximation comparison.

source.place: Tag 0DJE, lemma-tensor-pseudo-coherent, proof of (1), tensor approximation assertion (details omitted); expanded by the returned cone-triangle argument

proof.text: Apply the tensor approximation comparison to $\alpha,\beta,n,m,a,b$. It gives that $\alpha\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\beta:P\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q\to K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L$ is an isomorphism on cohomology above $t$ and surjective at $t$. Apply the finite-free total-model theorem to the chosen bounded complexes representing $P,Q$: their total tensor $E^\bullet$ is bounded finite free, and its image is isomorphic to $P\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q$. Compose this isomorphism with the comparison morphism. The resulting map $E^\bullet\to K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L$ has exactly the cohomology properties defining $t$-pseudo-coherence.

source.place: Tag 0DJE, lemma-tensor-pseudo-coherent, proof of (1), tensor approximation assertion (details omitted); expanded by the returned cone-triangle argument

proof.text: For pseudo-coherent $K,L$, the definition supplies bounded-above finite-free representatives $F^\bullet,G^\bullet$. The total-model theorem supplies a bounded-above finite-free complex $\operatorname{Tot}(F^\bullet\otimes_R G^\bullet)$ representing $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L$. This is precisely a pseudo-coherent representative in the cited definition, proving the last assertion.
